finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but discards the boolean result, so the authorization check is never enforced and any user can delete any account. The sibling closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, which throws.
finding.source: Any authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id (the id is attacker-controlled)

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) is the DELETE /accounts/{id} handler; id comes from the request
Account looked up by attacker-supplied id with no ownership filter
canDelete(u, a) result discarded, so no exception is thrown for non-owner non-admin

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (line 9-11) is correct but unused here. assertCanDelete (line 13-17) would throw but is not called. No other auth middleware or filter exists in the codebase (single file). The closeAccount path (line 29) does enforce the check, which confirms the omission in deleteAccount is a defect. An unknown id yields a null account and an NPE, which is not a bypass.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean but is called as a bare statement at line 22, so its result is discarded. assertCanDelete (13-17) throws but is only called in closeAccount (line 29). No other auth filter or middleware exists; the src/ directory contains only this file.
verdict.reason: src/AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete(u, a) as a bare statement with the boolean discarded, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user, regardless of ownership or admin status; closeAccount at line 29 uses the throwing assertCanDelete, which confirms the omission.
